content.title: About
content.content: Sweet potato fries are strips of batata (Ipomoea batatas) that are deep‑fried or baked until crisp. The tuber, native to Central and South America, has a naturally sweet flavor and bright orange flesh rich in beta‑carotene.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sweet potatoes contain two to three times more beta‑carotene than regular potatoes.
Sweet potato fries are often offered in fast‑food chains as a more nutritious alternative to classic fries.
Batata comes in several colors: orange, purple, yellow and white.
Unlike regular potatoes, sweet potatoes have a lower glycemic index, especially when baked.
The word “fries” comes from the French “frites,” meaning fried.

items.title: Rich in beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene converts to vitamin A, supporting vision, immunity and skin health.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium maintains electrolyte balance, normal blood pressure and heart function.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Sweet potatoes provide anthocyanins and vitamin C, which protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low in fat when baked
items.content: Baked sweet potato fries contain less saturated fat than traditional deep‑fried versions.

items.title: High carbohydrate content
items.content: Sweet potatoes are carbohydrate‑dense, so people with diabetes should monitor portion sizes.

items.title: Allergy to sweet potato
items.content: Although rare, some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to sweet potato.

items.title: Acrylamide formation during frying
items.content: Prolonged high‑temperature frying can produce acrylamides, compounds of potential concern.

items.title: Foodborne risk if stored improperly
items.content: Cut strips oxidize quickly and can harbor bacteria if left at room temperature for too long.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sweet potato fries are served hot as a side, snack, or accompaniment to main dishes. Sprinkle with salt, paprika, garlic powder or herbs. For a healthier option, bake the strips at 200 °C for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway through.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked fries in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Raw sweet potatoes keep best in a cool, dry place; sliced strips can be kept in water in the fridge, changing the water every 12 hours to prevent discoloration.
